input.quote: 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: No non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching covenant binds Customer anywhere in the Agreement: searches for "solicit", "induce", "recruit", "hire", "employ" and full review of § 12 (Customer Responsibilities), § 16 (Confidentiality) and § 30 (General) return no such restriction, and there is no restricted-period language (no "twelve (12) months" or "directly or indirectly" covenant). Section 12.3 affirmatively confirms the point in our favour, preserving Customer's freedom to hire any person responding to general recruitment (an express general-solicitation carve-out) and recording that Customer has made no no-hire commitment. This is our preferred position ("no non-solicit on Customer"), so no redline is proposed. The deterministic checks on duration (≤ 12 months) and a general-solicitation carve-out are inapplicable because there is no non-solicit clause to measure; the fallback (mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from the end of involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire) becomes relevant only if Vendor later proposes adding one.
